title: Wang-style integrated TE content and proliferation candidate
boundary: Review candidate, not a numbered manuscript figure. Six representatives are selected deterministically from overlap21: nearest to the 0%, 20%, 40%, 80%, and 100% conditional genome-size quantiles plus the D. fuscus anchor. Conditional genome size is IOD-derived and not a direct species C-value. Repeat proportions are fractions of aligned RepeatMasker hit bp, not genome occupancy; divergence bins are not insertion ages.
legend: Panel A prunes the supplied dated species tree to six deterministic overlap21 representatives. Panel B gives conditional D. fuscus-anchored genome size. Panels C-D show aligned-repeat composition for the six most abundant named biological orders plus Other, which includes the Unclassified annotation. Panel E shows zero-filled RepeatMasker divergence profiles on one common percentage scale.
alt_text: Six Desmognathus species are aligned across a dated phylogeny, conditional genome-size values, repeat-composition donuts, repeat-composition bars, and a seven-column grid of divergence profiles. Species rows and all data tracks share the same phylogenetic order.

title: Wang-style TE diversity and genome-size candidate
boundary: Review candidate, not a numbered manuscript figure. All genome-size values are conditional D. fuscus assembly-anchored IOD-derived estimates, not direct species C-values. Reproductive-strategy panels are post-hoc descriptive strata. The two direct developers are shown without a regression because n = 2.
legend: Rows show the canonical top-ten-superfamily Shannon entropy and Gini-Simpson index. Columns show all 21 overlap species, six aquatic-egg species, 13 terrestrial-egg species with aquatic larvae, and two direct developers. Hollow points are species and horizontal bars are conditional genome-size intervals. Lines and bands are Pagel-lambda PGLS fits and coefficient confidence bands; the n = 2 direct-development panels intentionally have no fit.
alt_text: Two aligned rows of four framed scatterplots show Shannon and Gini-Simpson diversity against conditional genome size for all Desmognathus and three reproductive strategies. PGLS statistics appear inside six panels; the two direct-development panels show only their two observations and state that a fit was not estimated.

title: Path24 development and phenotype reference
boundary: Descriptive review only. D. organi is absent from Path24 and is not imputed. The genome-size track uses conditional D. fuscus assembly-anchored pg/1C estimates, not direct independently measured species C-values. Tree time is shown as supplied; publication and calibration provenance remain unresolved.
legend: The supplied 24-tip Path24 dated tree is aligned to development mode and conditional D. fuscus-anchored genome-size, reviewed nucleus-area, and reviewed cell-area estimates. Horizontal bars are released conditional measurement intervals. The two sampled direct developers are D. aeneus and D. wrighti; the other 22 Path24 species have aquatic larvae and undergo metamorphosis. This is a descriptive visualization, not a development-mode test.
alt_text: A dated phylogeny for 24 Desmognathus species is aligned with a development-mode marker and forest-plot tracks for conditional genome size, nucleus area, and cell area. D. aeneus and D. wrighti are the two direct developers represented in Path24.

title: Path DAG equivalence-class reference
boundary: Not a numbered manuscript figure. The DAG node is Genome size on the conditional D. fuscus assembly-anchored pg/1C analysis, not a direct species C-value measurement. The same released genome-size scale is used consistently across all scored classes. The 10 testable equivalence classes do not orient a unique causal arrow; the saturated 6-member class is not shown and remains unscored because it has no d-separation claim.
legend: One representative DAG is shown for each of the 10 testable Path24 equivalence classes. Genome size denotes the conditional D. fuscus assembly-anchored pg/1C estimate, not a direct species C-value measurement. Equivalent arrow orientations are omitted, and the saturated 6-member class remains unscored.
alt_text: Ten boxed path diagrams connect Genome size, Nucleus area, and Cell area with arrows. Each is one representative of a testable equivalence class, not a uniquely oriented causal graph; the six-member saturated class is omitted as unscored.

title: Cross-study TE-diversity reference (Wang et al. 2025)
boundary: Descriptive cross-study context only; no pooled regression or hypothesis test is shown. Wang et al. 2025 published top-10 TE-superfamily indices are exact CC0-1.0 Dryad values (dataset DOI 10.5061/dryad.zpc866tkv; article DOI 10.1038/s42003-025-08127-3) produced from RepeatModeler/RepeatMasker annotations. Current top-10 indices are reclosed calculations from dnaPipeTE compositions. The pipelines are different and not method-harmonized. Current genome sizes are conditional D. fuscus assembly-anchored estimates, not direct species C-values.
legend: Panels A and C show genome size against top-ten-superfamily Shannon entropy and the Gini-Simpson index for 11 published salamanders and 21 current Desmognathus species. Panels B and D show the exact published vertebrate-group distributions beside all 34 current Desmognathus summaries. Wang et al. values come from RepeatModeler/RepeatMasker; current values come from dnaPipeTE. The comparison is descriptive and has no pooled fit.
alt_text: Two scatterplots compare genome size with top-ten-superfamily Shannon and Gini-Simpson diversity for published salamanders and current Desmognathus. Two aligned box-and-point panels compare nine vertebrate groups, highlighting published salamanders in blue and current Desmognathus in coral. No regression line or p-value is shown.
